title: Secure Parameters for the (2,3)-wPRF When n Equals s
summary: For the (2,3)-wPRF when n equals s, a subset-sum attack forces m far above twice s; finding concrete secure m values and resulting protocol efficiency remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the $(2,3)$-wPRF, analyze the alternative parameter regime $n=s$: a subset-sum attack resembling the attack on the $(2,3)$-OWF gives a lower bound on $m$ and indicates that $m$ must be much larger than $2s$, reducing protocol efficiency. Determine concrete secure values of $m$ and the resulting protocol efficiency while accounting for possible optimized subset-sum attacks that exploit the additional available data.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis and parameter selection for the (2,3)-wPRF under subset-sum attacks.
parameters: n: input-length parameter fixed equal to s in the alternative regime
s: security parameter and reference scale for n and m
m: construction parameter constrained by the subset-sum lower bound and protocol-efficiency tradeoff
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine concrete secure values of m and the resulting protocol efficiency when n equals s, accounting for optimized subset-sum attacks that exploit additional data.

citations.label: MPC-Friendly Symmetric Cryptography from Alternating Moduli: Candidates, Protocols, and Applications

progress.summary: The source gives a subset-sum-based lower bound indicating that m must be much larger than twice s in the n-equals-s regime, reducing efficiency. It leaves the concrete analysis to future work because optimizations exploiting additional data may be possible.
citation_labels: Itai Dinur et al., MPC-Friendly Symmetric Cryptography from Alternating Moduli: Candidates, Protocols, and Applications
